help.title: 📖 Bot help
help.description:
This bot connects the Discord server with the Roblox game: promo codes, eggs, events, gifts and more.
**For players:** `/codes` – active codes to type in the game • `/eggs` – eggs with pets and chances • `/events` – active events • `/leaderboard` – the game's top players.
help.config:
`/tutorial` – Step-by-step tutorial with live checks: start here.
`/setup` – Discord: language, the bug report channel and the log channel, diagnostics, the bot's servers.
`/setup-roblox` – Your Roblox game: connection, Studio file, names from the game, codes, eggs, events, gifts, bans, leaderboard, control panel.
`/setup-guide` – Answers to common questions.
help.codes:
`/code-add` – New code with rewards and validity (also sent to the game).
`/code-remove` – Remove one code or, without a code, several at once from a list.
`/sync-codes` – Send active codes to the game manually.

setup.sync_description: Codes added with `/code-add` are sent to the Roblox game automatically and work there right away, without publishing a game update. Requires an Open Cloud key (guide: `/setup-guide` → Codes in game).
setup.sync_key_steps:
1. create.roblox.com → Creator Dashboard → left menu **All tools** → **API Keys** → **Create API Key**
2. Name without spaces and without the word “Bot” (e.g. `apikey`), empty description
3. **universe-datastores** → add your game → `objects:create`, `objects:read`, `objects:update`, `control:create`
4. **messaging-service** → the same game → `universe-messaging-service:publish`
5. Security: IP restriction **off**, Expiration: **none**
6. **Save & Generate Key**, copy the key (shown only once) and click **Paste API key** below

kit.title: 📥 DiscordCodes.rbxmx in your game
kit.bot_version: The bot has file version **{version}** (bot folder → `scripts/DiscordCodes.rbxmx`).
kit.steps_title: How to replace the file (step by step)
kit.steps:
1. Open your game in Roblox Studio.
2. In **ServerScriptService** drag the old **DiscordCodes** into **ServerStorage** (a safe backup: scripts there do not run). Leave **DiscordSettings** where it is.
3. Right-click **ServerScriptService** → **Insert** → **Import Roblox Model** → pick `DiscordCodes.rbxmx` from the bot folder (the one with `start.bat`) → `scripts` folder. In older Studio: **Insert from File…**. Check that **DiscordCodes** is inside ServerScriptService (if it landed elsewhere, drag it there). No such option (new Studio)? Make your own tab with the **Model** tool: see `/tutorial` → *The Roblox Studio file*.
4. Click **Play**. The **Output** window should show `[DiscordCodes] File version …` and no red errors.
5. Publish the game (**File → Publish to Roblox**), in every place that has the file. When everything works, delete the backup from ServerStorage.
6. Join the game once and open `/setup-roblox`: it shows ✅.
kit.keep: **Stays untouched:** your own scripts (e.g. `CodeRewards` with `Core.OnReward`), the window `StarterGui → DiscordCodesGui` (the template), the catalog `DiscordCatalog` and your settings `DiscordSettings`. **Everything inside `DiscordCodes` is lost**, so change nothing in there: keep your own code in a separate script, your window design in the template and your settings in `DiscordSettings`. Did you change values in *DiscordCodes → Settings* of an older file? Insert `DiscordSettings.rbxmx` once and type them there (the backup in ServerStorage still shows them). Something broke after the update? Drag the old backup from ServerStorage back into ServerScriptService (and delete the new script).
kit.footer: The game reports its file version when a game server starts (joining the game or Play in Studio).

setup.sync_optional_scopes:
For **/roblox-ban**: the **user-restrictions** system → `universe.user-restriction:read` and `universe.user-restriction:write`.
For **/leaderboard**: the **ordered-data-store** system → `universe.ordered-data-store.scope.entry:read`.
Events, eggs, gifts and announcements use the same permissions as codes.

scan.warn_mult_currency: Your game code doesn't ask for the {currency} multiplier yet: the timer shows, but players won't get more. See /setup-roblox → ⚡ Events.
scan.warn_reward_currency: Your game has no number value named {currency}: this part of the reward can't be given yet.
scan.warn_reward_limit: Your game accepts at most **{limit}** currency at once (*DiscordSettings → MaxCurrencyPerCode*), and this reward has **{amount}** {currency}. The bot won't save it or send it to the game: start again with a smaller amount or raise the limit in the game.
scan.err_reward_limit:
❌ Your game accepts at most **{limit}** currency at once, and this reward has **{amount}** {currency}. The game wouldn't give it, so the bot saved nothing and nothing reached the game.
Lower the amount or raise the limit: Studio → *ServerScriptService → DiscordSettings → MaxCurrencyPerCode* (0 = no limit; no **DiscordSettings** there? Insert `DiscordSettings.rbxmx` from the bot's `scripts` folder once, next to DiscordCodes), then publish the game. The bot knows the limit from the game's latest report (published game or a Studio test) and sees a change a few minutes after a server starts with the new setting.
scan.warn_reward_exp: Your game has no EXP, XP or Experience value: the EXP part of the reward can't be given yet.
scan.warn_reward_item: Your game has no value named {item}: the item can't be given yet.
rbx.title: 🎮 Your Roblox game
rbx.description: Progress: **{done}/{total}** steps. Go from the top: steps 1–4 connect the game (once), the green buttons are the features. Not sure what to click? 📖 Tutorial.
rbx.game_missing: Press **🎮 Roblox game** and paste the link to your game.
rbx.connection_hint: Press **🔑 Game connection**: paste the API key, turn it on and press Test & sync.
rbx.kit_needs_connection: Finish step 2 first. Then insert `scripts/DiscordCodes.rbxmx` in Studio (📥 Studio file shows how).
rbx.scan_none: ❔ The game hasn't reported its names yet (insert the new Studio file, then press Play in Studio or join the game).
rbx.scan_ok: 🔍 The {where} reported {names} names and {spots} egg spots {time}.
rbx.sum_eggs: 🥚 Eggs: {count} active • egg spots in the game: {spots}
rbx.sum_events: ⚡ Events: {count} active • multipliers your game uses: {used}
rbx.sum_gifts_off: 🎁 Gifts and 📢 announcements: need the game connection (step 2)
rbx.footer: Changes work right away. Commands with more options: /egg-create, /event-start, /give, /roblox-ban.
rbx.codes_intro:
A player types a code in your game (the **Codes** button) and gets a reward. A new code works in the game within a few seconds, you don't publish the game.
Code: letters A–Z, digits, `_` and `-`, no spaces (e.g. `START2026`).
rbx.codes_none: No active codes yet. Click **➕ New code**.
rbx.codes_names_title: 💡 First: the names from your game
rbx.codes_names_hint: The form shows currencies and items as a list once the bot knows them: `/setup-roblox` → **🔍 What your game has** or **📒 Game catalog**. Without them you type the names yourself, exactly as they are in the game.
rbx.codes_footer: Commands work too: /code-add, /code-remove, /codes (the list for players)
rbx.code_validity: How long the code can be redeemed
rbx.no_scan_title: ❔ The bot doesn't know your game yet
rbx.no_scan_hint: Insert the new `scripts/DiscordCodes.rbxmx` in Studio (📥 Studio file), press **Play** and wait about a minute. Then the bot can check names here and warn you about options that can't work.
rbx.names_intro: Pick below which names from your game are **currencies**, **items/passes** and **pets**. The bot only uses names your game really has, so codes and eggs work. Names you typed by hand that aren't in the lists stay.
rbx.names_no_scan:
Your game hasn't reported its names yet.
1. Insert the new `scripts/DiscordCodes.rbxmx` in Studio (/setup-roblox → 📥 Studio file).
2. Turn on *File → Experience Settings → Security → Enable Studio Access to API Services*.
3. Press **Play** in Studio and wait about a minute.
4. Press **🔄 Refresh** here.
Until then you can type names by hand (**✏️ Type names**), exactly as in the game.
rbx.names_exp_missing: ⚠️ No EXP, XP or Experience value: EXP rewards won't work (unless your game uses Core.OnReward).
rbx.names_in_bot: 📋 Names set in the bot (✅ found in the game, ⚠️ not found)
rbx.names_none_in_bot: None yet: pick them in the lists below.
rbx.names_hook_reward: ✅ Your game gives rewards itself (Core.OnReward), so any names it knows work.
rbx.names_hooks: 🔧 Your own functions in the game
rbx.names_no_hooks: None (the automatic mode looks for values named like the reward).
rbx.names_footer: Only names are reported, never amounts or usernames. Data from players on one server; values a player doesn't have yet don't show.
rbx.names_more: Lists show the first {max} names; type the rest with ✏️ Type names.
rbx.eggs_intro: An egg stands in your game on a spot tagged `DiscordEggSpot`. A player pays with a currency and hatches a pet. Below you can see what your game has for eggs.
rbx.eggs_spots: 📍 Egg spots in the game (tag DiscordEggSpot)
rbx.eggs_spots_none: ⚠️ None. In Studio select a Part → Properties → Tags → + → `DiscordEggSpot`, then publish the game.
rbx.eggs_models_none: None: a simple colored egg is used.
rbx.eggs_pets: 🐾 How a pet gets to the player
rbx.eggs_pets_hook: ✅ Your game has its own pet system (Live.OnHatch): any pet names it knows work.
rbx.eggs_pets_values: The pet goes into the value named like it in player data (e.g. `Pets.Dragon`). Your pets (✅ found in the game, ⚠️ not found):
rbx.eggs_pets_none: No pets set: pick them in 🔍 What your game has.
rbx.eggs_pay_hook: ✅ Your game takes the price itself (Core.OnSpend).
rbx.eggs_pay_values: The price is taken from the currency value. Your currencies:
rbx.eggs_footer: Color, time and model are set under the finished egg • the commands work too: /egg-create, /egg-edit
rbx.egg_pick_preset: Which egg of your game should I copy? Its pets and chances fill in by themselves, and you can still change everything.
rbx.egg_pets_too_long: Too long for this form: leave empty (no change) or use /egg-edit
rbx.egg_preset_too_long: ❌ The pet list of **{name}** is too long for the form. Use `/egg-create` and pick it in the suggestions of `pets`.
rbx.egg_presets_limited: The list shows the first 25 of {total} catalog eggs; the others: /egg-create.
rbx.egg_pick_edit: Which egg do you want to change?
rbx.egg_no_presets: The game catalog lists no eggs yet. Add them in DiscordCatalog: /setup-roblox → 📒 Game catalog.
rbx.egg_done_footer: Color, time and model: the menus below change them at once.
rbx.err_price: ❌ Type the price as a number above 0, e.g. 500.
rbx.events_intro: An event turns on a multiplier on every game server for a chosen time; players see a timer. Luck in eggs always works. Currency and EXP only work if your game code asks for them (✅ below).
rbx.events_how: How to turn on a currency or EXP multiplier in the game
rbx.events_code:
Your developer (or an AI helping with your game) adds one line where the game gives currency or EXP:
```lua
local Live = require(game.ServerScriptService:WaitForChild("DiscordCodes"):WaitForChild("Live"))
amount = amount * Live.GetMultiplier("Coins")   -- or "EXP"
```
After a game server runs that line once, it shows ✅ here.
rbx.event_pick_animation: ⚡ **New event**: first pick the animation the players will see. Then the form with the name, time and multiplier opens.
rbx.event_no_animation_desc: Only the event's icon and timer in the game
rbx.event_anim_desc.coin_storm: Gold coins rain around every player (currency)
rbx.event_anim_desc.aurora: Night with an aurora and EXP orbs (EXP)
rbx.event_anim_desc.lucky_breeze: Golden hour, clovers and a rainbow (luck in eggs)
rbx.event_anim_desc.meteor_shower: Dusk, a planet and meteors (Gems or a big event)
rbx.event_anim_desc.sakura_festival: Sunset, cherry trees and lanterns (everything x2)
rbx.event_custom_duration: Or type your own time (instead of the list)
rbx.event_custom_duration_ph: e.g. 45m, 2h30m, 2d (empty = the time from the list above)
rbx.event_kind: What to multiply (pick one or more)
rbx.event_more_options: Different multipliers for different things (e.g. 2× Coins and 3× EXP): /event-start
rbx.mult_missing: the timer shows, but the game doesn't multiply it yet
rbx.mult_unknown: can't check yet (the game hasn't reported)
rbx.mult_all_desc: every currency your game asks a multiplier for
rbx.mult_luck_desc: always works: rare pets (5% and less) more likely
rbx.gifts_intro:
**Gift:** a reward for one player without a code; an offline player gets it when they join.
**Announcement:** a message on every player's screen, filtered by Roblox.
rbx.gifts_places: Where gifts go in your game
rbx.gifts_places_auto: Currencies and items go into values named like them (see 🔍 What your game has).
rbx.gifts_commands_text:
`/give` – the same in one command (username or Roblox ID, with EXP and item time), sent at once, no draft
`/announce-game` – announcement
rbx.gift_item_hint: EXP and the item's time (e.g. VIP for 24 h) come after Submit, with ⚙️ in the draft.
rbx.announce_text_ph: No links: Roblox would hide the whole announcement (####)
rbx.bans_intro: Ban a player on every server of your game, for a time or forever, through Roblox's official ban system. It works in the published game (not in Studio). The easiest way: **🔍 Find a player** below opens the player card with **Ban**, **Unban** and **Send a gift**.
rbx.bans_permission_text: Creator Hub → API Keys → your key → Access Permissions → **user-restrictions** → your game → `universe.user-restriction:read` and `universe.user-restriction:write` → Save Changes. Test on a second account, never your own.
rbx.bans_commands:
`/roblox-ban` – ban (time, reason shown to the player)
`/roblox-unban` – unban
`/roblox-ban-check` – check a player
rbx.board_intro: `/leaderboard` shows the top players of your game on Discord. The bot reads your game's own leaderboard (an OrderedDataStore).
rbx.board_find_text: In your game's leaderboard script look for `GetOrderedDataStore("NAME")`: NAME is what you paste. The API key needs **ordered-data-store** → `universe.ordered-data-store.scope.entry:read`. No such script? Your game has no global leaderboard yet.

rbx.chk_publish_error: ⚠️ Instant messages: {error} (the game still refreshes every minute)
rbx.chk_kit_unknown: ⚠️ Can't check the file in the game

rbx.chk_currencies_ok: ✅ All currencies found in the game
rbx.chk_currencies_missing: ⚠️ Currencies not found in the game: {names}

tut.chk_perms_ok: The bot has every permission it needs

tut.chk_scan_missing: The game hasn't reported its names yet

welcome.title: 👋 Thanks for adding me!
welcome.description: I connect this Discord server with your Roblox game: promo codes, eggs, events, gifts, on-screen announcements, bans and more.
welcome.steps:
1. **`/tutorial`** – a step-by-step tutorial that shows what is already set up.
2. **`/setup`** – Discord: language and the bug report channel.
3. **`/setup-roblox`** – your Roblox game: connection, Studio file, codes, eggs, events.
`/setup-guide` has answers to common questions.
welcome.footer: Change the bot language in /setup → the 🌐 Language / Język / Idioma list.
rbx.sum_codes: 📜 Promo codes: {count} active (button **Promo codes** below or `/code-add`)
errors.bot_not_in_server:
❌ I'm not added to this server as a bot, so I can't see its roles and channels. Add me with this link (choose this server): {invite}
Then type the command again.
errors.not_home_guild: ❌ This bot works only on its owner's servers and this server isn't on the list. The bot's owner can add it in /setup → 🌐 Servers.
errors.server_only: ❌ The bot's commands work only on a server, not in direct messages.
errors.starting: ⏳ The bot is still starting. Try again in a few seconds.
errors.bot_forbidden: ❌ Discord didn't let the bot do this: it is missing a permission in this channel, or its role is too low. /setup → 🩺 Diagnostics shows what to fix.
errors.bot_missing: ❌ The bot is missing these permissions here: {perms}. Give them to the bot's role (Server Settings → Roles) or in this channel's settings.
kit.window: After you insert the file, players see a purple **Codes** button on the left edge of the screen: they click it, type the code and press **Redeem**. Want your own look (colors, texts, size)? Insert the template **once**: right-click **StarterGui** → **Insert** → **Import Roblox Model** → `DiscordCodesWindow.rbxmx` from the `scripts` folder. You edit it like any window in Studio and updates never touch it. To hide or move the button or change the language, insert `DiscordSettings.rbxmx` once, next to DiscordCodes (`/setup-guide` → *Codes in game: Studio install*). Details: `/tutorial` → *Code window in the game*.
catalog.title: 📒 Game catalog
catalog.description_ok: Your game reported its catalog {time} ({where}). The bot's commands suggest these names and refuse names that aren't here, so a typo can't create a code that doesn't work.
catalog.description_missing: Your game has no catalog yet. Without it the bot only knows the names players happen to have in their data, so a typo can easily create a code that won't work in the game. Add the catalog once (below) and the bot will know the exact names.
catalog.description_unknown: The game hasn't reported a catalog yet. Usually it has an older DiscordCodes file (replace it: **📥 Studio file**) or nobody started the game since. Click **Play** in Studio and refresh.
catalog.robux_empty: Empty. If players can buy a currency, item or pet with Robux, list it in `Catalog.SoldForRobux`: the bot then warns you about rewards from that list (Roblox rules on codes).
catalog.robux_warning: {names}: bought with Robux in your game (game catalog). Roblox doesn't allow giving this in codes posted outside Roblox (e.g. on Discord) or as a prize of a contest outside Roblox.
catalog.howto_title: 📥 How to add the catalog (once, no coding)
catalog.howto:
1. In Roblox Studio right-click **ServerScriptService** → **Insert** → **Import Roblox Model** → the file `DiscordCatalog.rbxmx` from the bot folder → `scripts` folder.
2. Double-click **DiscordCatalog** and replace the examples with the names from your game, exactly as the game spells them.
3. Click **Play**: the **Output** window shows `[DiscordCodes] Game catalog: …`. Then publish the game.
4. Come back here and click **🔄 Refresh**.
You need the current DiscordCodes file (**📥 Studio file**). Don't know the names? Click **🤖 Text for an AI assistant**.
catalog.footer: The catalog is yours: updates of the DiscordCodes file never touch it. Only names go to the bot.
catalog.ai_intro: Copy the text below and paste it into your AI assistant together with the game scripts that hold your lists. Paste the finished module into **DiscordCatalog** in ServerScriptService.
catalog.ai_names: Names the game already reported to the bot (from player data): {names}
catalog.err_currencies: ❌ Your game's catalog has no currency “{name}”.
catalog.err_items: ❌ Your game's catalog has no item “{name}”.
catalog.err_reward_item: ❌ Your game's catalog has no “{name}” among the things a player can get.
catalog.err_pets: ❌ Your game's catalog has no pet “{name}”.
catalog.err_multipliers: ❌ Your game's catalog has no multiplier “{name}”.
catalog.err_hint: 💡 The names come from the **DiscordCatalog** module in your game. Something missing? Add it there, click **Play** (or publish the game), then `/setup-roblox` → **📒 Game catalog** → **🔄 Refresh**.
catalog.summary_unknown: 📒 Game catalog: not reported by the game yet.
catalog.summary_missing: 📒 No game catalog: add it (**📒 Game catalog**) so the bot knows the exact names.
catalog.summary_ok: 📒 Game catalog: currencies {currencies}, items {items}, pets {pets}, eggs {eggs}, multipliers {multipliers}.
catalog.problem.not_list: **{what}** must be a list of names.
catalog.problem.bad_name: **{what}**, entry {detail}: this is not a name (empty text?).
catalog.problem.too_many: **{what}**: the bot only gets the first {detail}.
catalog.problem.error: The module has an error: `{detail}`. The Output window in Studio shows the line.
catalog.problem.no_return: The module must end with the line `return Catalog`.
catalog.problem.egg_unknown_pets: The egg **{egg}** has pets that aren't in `Catalog.Pets`: {pets}.
catalog.problem.egg_unknown_currency: The egg **{egg}** costs the currency **{currency}**, which isn't in `Catalog.Currencies`.
catalog.chk_unknown: ⚠️ 📒 The game hasn't reported a catalog (an older DiscordCodes file, or nobody started the game).
catalog.chk_missing: 💡 📒 The game has no catalog. It's optional, but with it the bot knows the exact names: `/setup-roblox` → **📒 Game catalog**.
catalog.chk_code_unknown: ⚠️ 🔑 The code `{code}` gives “{name}”, which isn't in the game catalog. Players can't redeem it until you fix the name.
catalog.chk_code_robux: ⚠️ 💎 Code `{code}` gives {names}, which players buy with Robux (game catalog). Roblox doesn't allow that in codes posted outside Roblox (e.g. on Discord).
catalog.chk_egg_unknown: ⚠️ 🥚 The egg **{egg}** uses names that aren't in the catalog: {names}.
tut.chk_gpanel_missing: The control panel is not posted yet
tut.chk_gpanel_admins_only: Only administrators use the panel (no roles chosen)
tut.chk_home_ok: This server is on the bot's list
tut.chk_home_missing: This server isn't on the bot's list: /setup → 🌐 Servers
tut.chk_public_off: Public Bot is off: only you can add the bot
tut.chk_public_on: Public Bot is ON: turn it off (Developer Portal → Installation, then Bot)
tut.no_chapters: The tutorial file can't be read. Put back locales/tutorial_*.json from the bot package or the last update.
rbx.names_source: ℹ️ Your game sent these names: the DiscordCodes file reads them from player data while someone plays (also **Play** in Studio). Only names, never amounts or usernames, saved in your game's DataStore and read with your API key. `@` before a name = a player attribute.
rbx.names_cut: ⚠️ Only the first {max} names were kept.
catalog.problem.name_too_long: **{what}**: the name “{detail}…” is longer than 100 characters. Shorten it in the game and in the catalog.
catalog.problem.timeout: The module takes longer than {detail} s to load, so the bot skipped it. Usually it waits with `WaitForChild` for something that isn't there: add a limit, e.g. `WaitForChild("GameConfig", 10)`.
catalog.problem.egg_missing_chances: The egg **{egg}**: only some pets have a chance. Give every pet a chance (or none, then they're equal).
catalog.problem.robux_unknown: SoldForRobux has names the other lists don't: {names}. Check the spelling, or the bot can't warn about them.
catalog.note_catalog_wins: ℹ️ Your game has a catalog with this list, so the commands use the catalog's names. Add a new name to **DiscordCatalog** in the game.
catalog.summary_template: 📒 Catalog: still only the template's example names – fill it in (/setup-roblox → 📒 Game catalog)
catalog.problem.template: The catalog still has only the template's example names (Coins, Gems, VIP Pass, Speed Coil…). Type your game's real names into DiscordCatalog; until then the bot doesn't use it to check names.
access.private_bot: 👋 This is a private bot: it works only on its owner's servers, so it is leaving this server now. Is it your bot? Add this server in /setup → 🌐 Servers on your main server, or make the bot's owner (the Discord account that created the bot) an administrator here, then invite the bot again.
access.console_unknown: Could not check whether server {guild} belongs to the bot's owner (Discord didn't answer). The bot ignores it until the next start.
access.console_public: "Public Bot" is ON in the Discord Developer Portal: anyone can try to add this bot (it leaves such servers by itself, but turn it off): discord.com/developers/applications → your app → first Installation: set Install Link to None and untick User Install → Save Changes; then Bot → turn Public Bot off → Save Changes.
servers.title: 🌐 The bot's servers
servers.description: The bot's settings are shared by all its servers, so the bot works only on its owner's servers. A server is added by itself when the bot's owner (the Discord account that created the bot in the Developer Portal) owns it or has **Administrator** or **Manage Server** there. On any other server the bot leaves.
servers.not_joined: the bot is not there yet
servers.strangers: ⚠️ The bot is there, but it isn't on the list
servers.public_on: ⚠️ **Public Bot is ON**: anyone can try to add the bot. Turn it off: **discord.com/developers/applications** → your app → first **Installation**: set **Install Link** to **None** and untick **User Install** → **Save Changes**; then **Bot** → turn **Public Bot** off → **Save Changes**.
servers.public_off: ✅ Public Bot is off: only you can add the bot.
servers.footer: Only the bot's owner can change this list.
servers.add_title: Add a server before inviting the bot
servers.bad_id: ❌ A server ID has 17–20 digits. Turn on Developer Mode (User Settings → Advanced), then right-click the server → **Copy Server ID**.
servers.added: ✅ Server `{guild}` was added. Now invite the bot there: it will stay.
servers.removed: ✅ {guild} was removed from the list and the bot left it.
servers.owner_only: ❌ Only the bot's owner (the Discord account that created the bot in the Developer Portal) can change the list of servers.
startup.no_token:
❌ ERROR: No valid DISCORD_TOKEN in the .env file!
👉 Open .env and paste your bot token from the Discord Developer Portal (your app → Bot → Reset Token).
startup.bad_token: ❌ Discord didn't accept the bot token (DISCORD_TOKEN in .env). Get a new one: Developer Portal → your app → Bot → Reset Token, paste it into .env and start the bot again.
startup.intents: ❌ Discord refused the connection: the bot needs one intent. Developer Portal → your app → Bot → turn on SERVER MEMBERS INTENT → Save Changes, then start the bot again.
startup.no_internet: ⚠️ No connection to Discord ({error}). Trying again in {seconds} s...
startup.config_broken:
❌ config.json can't be read: {error}
👉 Open {path} in Notepad and fix the mistake (often a missing comma or quote), or put back your copy. Nothing was changed.
startup.database_error:
❌ The database (data/bot.db) can't be opened: {error}
👉 Make sure no other program uses it. Copies are in data/backups.
startup.already_running: ❌ This bot is already running (another start.bat window, or another program started it). Close the other one first: two copies would answer everything twice.
startup.env_override: ⚠️ {name} is also set in the system (outside .env); the value from .env is used.
startup.sync_failed: ⚠️ The bot couldn't send its slash commands to Discord: {error}. New or changed commands may be missing until the next start.
startup.env_broken_line: ⚠️ Line {line} of the .env file ({start}…) has no “=”, so the bot ignores it. Write it as NAME=value, e.g. DISCORD_TOKEN=your_token (no spaces).
startup.updated: 🔄 The bot was updated from version {old} to {new}. What changed: the file CHANGELOG.md in the bot folder.
grequest.author: {name} (in the game)
grequest.bad: The request is missing something or has a wrong value. Fill in the form again.
grequest.code_exists: The code {code} is already active. Remove it first or choose another name.
grequest.unknown: The bot doesn't know this request. Update the bot and the Studio file to the same version.
grequest.too_old: The bot was off when you sent this, so nothing was done. Send it again.
grequest.error: Something went wrong in the bot. Nothing more was done; the details are in the bot's window.
grequest.ban_link: The reason has a link, which Roblox would hide from the player. Write it without the link.
grequest.found: Account: {username} (ID {user_id}). Check it, then click Ban to ban exactly this account.
panellog.skipped: 🎮 {count} earlier change(s) from the game's ⚙️ Manager are not listed here: the game keeps only the newest 100, and a bot reading a game for the first time lists only the newest 10.
sync.busy: The game was changing this data at the same moment several times in a row. The bot tries again in a moment by itself.

perm.title: 🛡️ Permissions
perm.hub_description:
**Administrators** may always do everything. Here you give access to other people, and for each of them you tick **exactly what they may do**:

💬 **What each role may do** – Discord roles (e.g. Moderator): the game commands (`/code-add`, `/give`, `/event-start`, `/roblox-ban`…) and the buttons of the 🕹️ control panel.
🎮 **Manager in the game** – Roblox players who may open the ⚙️ Manager in your game (its owner always can).

The bot's settings (`/setup`, `/setup-roblox`) stay for administrators only.
perm.roles_description:
1. In the **first list** pick the roles that get access (e.g. Moderator).
2. In the **second list** pick one of them.
3. In the **third list** tick what that role may do. A role with nothing ticked can't do anything yet.

A member with several roles may do everything their roles allow together.
perm.roles_placeholder: Roles with access to the game
perm.pick_role: Pick a role to set its permissions
perm.roles_field: Roles and what they may do
perm.roles_footer: A change works at once: the next click of that person is checked again.
perm.game_description:
Who may open the **⚙️ Manager** in your Roblox game besides its owner (the owner may always do everything).
1. **➕ Add a player** and type their Roblox username.
2. Pick them in the first list and tick what they may do.

The list goes to the game by itself (the game connection must be on: `/setup-roblox` → Game connection). The person gets the ⚙️ Manager button the next time they join, or within a minute if they are playing; they see only the tabs of what they may do (and Start).

You can also do this in the game itself: the owner opens ⚙️ Manager → 🛡️ tab, finds a player by name and ticks what they may do. It is one list: a change there shows here too.
